claim: Two stacked panels compare context retrieval and reconstruction, then show iteration through tools, observations and revision.
caption: **Two ways to steer an agent.** (a) Purposeful representations can reduce the effort needed to recover relevant system knowledge. (b) Feedback loops let agents revise their work using observations from tools and checks. Both can improve performance without changing the foundation model, but neither guarantees an acceptable result.
topology: Two stacked panels compare context retrieval and reconstruction, then show iteration through tools, observations and revision.
grayscale: Black outlines, white panels and black arrows.
required_terms: Repeat until acceptance criteria are met or work stops
alt: Two ways to steer an agent. Panel (a) compares reconstructing relevant structure from raw code at higher cost with retrieving it from a purposeful representation at lower cost. Panel (b) shows a loop from proposing a change through running tools, observing results, and revising. It repeats until acceptance criteria are met or work stops.
